The number formats fixture (KERNEL.47). Each case sits under a line
"=== <name>" and runs to the next such line; these lines before the first
header are ignored. A case's first line is a format code as
Range.NumberFormat takes it, written as it is, quotes and all; each line
after it is a value the code draws, a number in the record's spelling or a
text after an apostrophe ('abc), Excel's own mark for a text. A header that
ends "!refused <words>" names a code this version does not draw, the words
being ones its refusal names (grid-format-code); such a case carries no
value. VlaWriteFormatsGolden (VLA_Tests.bas) has Excel draw every case and
writes formats_golden.txt beside this file: the header, then
"CODE<TAB><the code as Range.NumberFormat reads it back>" or
"REFUSED<TAB><Excel's error number>", then one line a value, "<the value as
written><TAB><Range.Text in a column 255 characters wide>". vla-lang's
numfmt.rs is held to that file by its own test (tests/formats_golden.rs),
over the crate's copies, and tools/check_formats_golden.ps1 holds the
pair's shape and the constructs the cases reach.
